newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares sharply higher after lively trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares sharply higher after lively trade.

text.p: German shares were sharply higher in afternoon electronic trade on Tuesday, lifted by a dollar recovery and the ongoing effects of a firmer close on Wall Street.

Dealers said the strength of the German debt market and firm futures also underpinned trade, and the IBIS DAX index, which measures trade in 30 German blue-chips, ended the day at 3,233.34 points, up 52.71 points or 1.66 percent.
"This is really the follow through from Wall Street yesterday. The Street isn't really doing that much today, but a lot of stocks seem better on sentiment," a trader said.
The DAX index ended the day earlier at 3,233.21 points, up 49 points or 1.54 percent.
Volkswagen AG shares were weaker than the market over the day and fell back considerably when the carmaker released weaker-than-expected group earnings for 1996 of 678 million marks.
VW shares traded at 803.70 marks when the figures were released, but quickly fell back and ended at 787.40 marks, down 8.60 marks.

Dealers said there was keen interest in the steel sector over the day, particularly Thyssen AG, which ended up 14.60 marks at 349 marks on the back of a Deutsche MG analysts' upgrade of the stock on Monday.
"A lot of shares seem better on sentiment, like the utility stocks, which are enjoying a sector rotation," a trader said.
Veba AG shares ended up two marks at 96.85 marks, shares in Viag AG ended up 14.30 marks at 726, while RWE AG ended up 1.05 marks at 74.05 marks.
Insurer Allianz AG saw a surge in profits at its domestic non-life unit and shares rose accordingly on the news. Shares fell slightly later on, and ended the day up 64 marks at 3,288 marks.
